claim: The zebrafish psoriasis mutant was isolated in a phenotype-based screen after undirected ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-mutagenesis.
source: The zebrafish psoriasis mutant was isolated in a phenotype-based screen after undirected ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-mutagenesis and has been described as developing edema as well as epidermal aggregates during embryogenesis (Figure 1a,b) (Webb et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites Webb et al., 2008 as the source of this information about the mutant isolation.

claim: The psoriasis mutant develops edema during embryogenesis.
source: The zebrafish psoriasis mutant was isolated in a phenotype-based screen after undirected ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-mutagenesis and has been described as developing edema as well as epidermal aggregates during embryogenesis (Figure 1a,b) (Webb et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Webb et al., 2008 and by Figure 1a,b showing the phenotype.

claim: The psoriasis mutant develops epidermal aggregates during embryogenesis.
source: The zebrafish psoriasis mutant was isolated in a phenotype-based screen after undirected ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS)-mutagenesis and has been described as developing edema as well as epidermal aggregates during embryogenesis (Figure 1a,b) (Webb et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Webb et al., 2008 and by Figure 1a,b showing the phenotype.

claim: Aggregates in psoriasis mutants are preferentially found on the median fin folds.
source: Aggregates were preferentially found on the median fin folds, but also on the flanks, the yolk sac and the head (Figure 1c–g).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1c-g.

claim: Aggregates in psoriasis mutants are also found on the flanks, the yolk sac and the head.
source: Aggregates were preferentially found on the median fin folds, but also on the flanks, the yolk sac and the head (Figure 1c–g).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1c-g.

claim: The aggregates in psoriasis mutants consist of both peridermal cells and basal keratinocytes.
source: Analysis with specific molecular markers revealed that the aggregates consist of both peridermal cells and basal keratinocytes (see Figure 1h for schematic of embryonic skin), and can already be detected at 48 hours post-fertilization (hpf) (Figure 1i–k).
evidence: The claim is supported by molecular marker analysis shown in Figure 1i-k.

claim: Aggregates in psoriasis mutants can be detected at 48 hours post-fertilization.
source: Analysis with specific molecular markers revealed that the aggregates consist of both peridermal cells and basal keratinocytes (see Figure 1h for schematic of embryonic skin), and can already be detected at 48 hours post-fertilization (hpf) (Figure 1i–k).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1i-k.

claim: Initial defects in psoriasis mutants are more pronounced in the outer periderm.
source: Initial defects were more pronounced in the outer periderm, in which the normally flat cells started to round up (Figure 1i,j).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1i,j.

claim: Normally flat peridermal cells start to round up in psoriasis mutants.
source: Initial defects were more pronounced in the outer periderm, in which the normally flat cells started to round up (Figure 1i,j).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1i,j.

claim: Cell membranes in peridermal cells of psoriasis mutants display reduced levels of E-cadherin (Cdh1), particularly in basal domains facing the underlying basal keratinocytes.
source: In addition, cell membranes, in particular in basal domains facing the underlying basal keratinocytes, displayed reduced levels of the cell-cell adhesion molecule E-cadherin (Cdh1) (Figure 1i',j').
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1i',j'.

claim: Altered organization of basal keratinocytes in psoriasis mutants is only obvious in more advanced aggregates.
source: Altered organization of basal keratinocytes themselves was only obvious in more advanced aggregates, in which cells had lost their regular epithelial shape and their mono-layered organization (Figure 1k).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1k.

claim: In advanced aggregates of psoriasis mutants, basal keratinocytes lose their regular epithelial shape.
source: Altered organization of basal keratinocytes themselves was only obvious in more advanced aggregates, in which cells had lost their regular epithelial shape and their mono-layered organization (Figure 1k).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1k.

claim: In advanced aggregates of psoriasis mutants, basal keratinocytes lose their mono-layered organization.
source: Altered organization of basal keratinocytes themselves was only obvious in more advanced aggregates, in which cells had lost their regular epithelial shape and their mono-layered organization (Figure 1k).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1k.

claim: At 56 hpf, hyper-proliferation is evident in basal cells of psoriasis mutants.
source: At 56 hpf, hyper-proliferation was evident in basal cells, whereas peridermal cells did not proliferate (Figure 1l,m).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 1l,m.

claim: At 56 hpf, peridermal cells of psoriasis mutants do not proliferate.
source: At 56 hpf, hyper-proliferation was evident in basal cells, whereas peridermal cells did not proliferate (Figure 1l,m).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 1l,m.

claim: Basal keratinocytes of psoriasis mutants undergo partial epithelial-mesenchymal transitions at 48 hpf.
source: Live time-lapse imaging revealed partial epithelial-mesenchymal transitions (EMTs) in the basal keratinocytes of mutant embryos at 48 hpf, characterized by the formation of cellular processes and dynamic dissociations and re-associations of cells (Figure 2a,b and Videos 1,2).
evidence: The claim is supported by live time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2a,b and Videos 1,2.

claim: Partial epithelial-mesenchymal transitions in psoriasis mutants are characterized by the formation of cellular processes.
source: Live time-lapse imaging revealed partial epithelial-mesenchymal transitions (EMTs) in the basal keratinocytes of mutant embryos at 48 hpf, characterized by the formation of cellular processes and dynamic dissociations and re-associations of cells (Figure 2a,b and Videos 1,2).
evidence: The claim is supported by live time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2a,b and Videos 1,2.

claim: Partial epithelial-mesenchymal transitions in psoriasis mutants are characterized by dynamic dissociations and re-associations of cells.
source: Live time-lapse imaging revealed partial epithelial-mesenchymal transitions (EMTs) in the basal keratinocytes of mutant embryos at 48 hpf, characterized by the formation of cellular processes and dynamic dissociations and re-associations of cells (Figure 2a,b and Videos 1,2).
evidence: The claim is supported by live time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2a,b and Videos 1,2.

claim: At 58 hpf, basal keratinocytes of psoriasis mutants have loosened their intercellular connections.
source: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and immunofluorescence (IF) analyses of the median fin folds of psoriasis mutants revealed that at 58 hpf basal keratinocytes had loosened their intercellular connections (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: The claim is supported by TEM and IF data shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: The basement membrane underneath the basal layer of psoriasis mutants is disintegrated to variable degrees at 58 hpf.
source: In addition, the basement membrane (BM) underneath the basal layer was disintegrated to variable degrees (Figure 2e–j; Figure 2—figure supplement1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2e-j and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Numerous basal cells of psoriasis mutants have entered the dermal compartment at 58 hpf.
source: Furthermore, numerous basal cells had entered the dermal compartment (Figure 2i,j) where they were in close contact with the remnants of the actinotrichia, dermal collagenous structures that were significantly disassembled in regions with epidermal aggregates (Figure 2c,d,g,h; Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2i,j.

claim: Basal cells that enter the dermal compartment in psoriasis mutants are in close contact with the remnants of the actinotrichia.
source: Furthermore, numerous basal cells had entered the dermal compartment (Figure 2i,j) where they were in close contact with the remnants of the actinotrichia, dermal collagenous structures that were significantly disassembled in regions with epidermal aggregates (Figure 2c,d,g,h; Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2i,j.

claim: Actinotrichia are significantly disassembled in regions with epidermal aggregates in psoriasis mutants.
source: Furthermore, numerous basal cells had entered the dermal compartment (Figure 2i,j) where they were in close contact with the remnants of the actinotrichia, dermal collagenous structures that were significantly disassembled in regions with epidermal aggregates (Figure 2c,d,g,h; Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2c,d,g,h and Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-d.

claim: Basal keratinocytes of psoriasis mutants display both hyperplasia and invasive behavior.
source: Together, this evidence demonstrates that basal keratinocytes of psoriasis mutants display both hyperplasia and invasive behavior, characteristics of epidermal malignancy.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined evidence of hyperproliferation and invasion into dermal compartments.

claim: Hyperplasia and invasive behavior are characteristics of epidermal malignancy.
source: Together, this evidence demonstrates that basal keratinocytes of psoriasis mutants display both hyperplasia and invasive behavior, characteristics of epidermal malignancy.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about cancer characteristics.

claim: psoriasis mutants display moderate skin inflammation characterized by increased numbers of mpx-positive neutrophils at 54 hpf.
source: In addition, psoriasis mutants displayed moderate skin inflammation, characterized by increased numbers of mpx-positive neutrophils and lyz-positive macrophages at 54 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a,c; and data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a,c.

claim: psoriasis mutants display moderate skin inflammation characterized by increased numbers of lyz-positive macrophages at 54 hpf.
source: In addition, psoriasis mutants displayed moderate skin inflammation, characterized by increased numbers of mpx-positive neutrophils and lyz-positive macrophages at 54 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a,c; and data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text but the data is not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Inflammation does not contribute to epidermal malignancy in psoriasis mutants.
source: This inflammation does not, however, seem to contribute to epidermal malignancy, as epidermal aggregates of unaltered numbers and sizes were also obtained in psoriasis mutants after ablation of the myeloid lineage by pu.1 antisense morpholino oligonucleotide (MO) injection (Carney et al., 2007) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–e).
evidence: The claim is supported by data showing that ablation of the myeloid lineage does not prevent epidermal aggregates, as shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a-e.

claim: Epidermal aggregates of unaltered numbers and sizes are obtained in psoriasis mutants after ablation of the myeloid lineage by pu.1 MO injection.
source: This inflammation does not, however, seem to contribute to epidermal malignancy, as epidermal aggregates of unaltered numbers and sizes were also obtained in psoriasis mutants after ablation of the myeloid lineage by pu.1 antisense morpholino oligonucleotide (MO) injection (Carney et al., 2007) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–e).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a-e and cites Carney et al., 2007 for the pu.1 MO method.

claim: Webb et al. placed the psoriasis mutation within a defined region on LG 6 through meiotic mapping.
source: Applying meiotic mapping, Webb et al. had placed the psoriasis mutation within a defined region on LG 6, but the causing lesion had not been identified (Webb et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim cites Webb et al., 2008 as the source of the mapping information.

claim: The causing lesion of the psoriasis mutation had not been identified by Webb et al.
source: Applying meiotic mapping, Webb et al. had placed the psoriasis mutation within a defined region on LG 6, but the causing lesion had not been identified (Webb et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim cites Webb et al., 2008 as the source of this information.

claim: Whole exome sequencing of pooled mutant siblings and their parents confirmed linkage to LG 6.
source: We conducted whole exome sequencing of pooled mutant siblings and their (heterozygous) parents and confirmed the linkage to LG 6 (Figure 3a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by exome sequencing data shown in Figure 3a,b.

claim: A C to T transition was identified in exon 6 of the gene atp1b1a.
source: In addition, we identified a C to T transition in exon 6 of the gene atp1b1a, which was confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The C to T transition in atp1b1a was confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
source: In addition, we identified a C to T transition in exon 6 of the gene atp1b1a, which was confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by Sanger sequencing data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Exons of all other annotated genes in the region around atp1b1a contained no nonsense, non-conservative missense or splice site mutations.
source: By contrast, exons of all other annotated genes in this region (from 1.32 Mb / 22 genes North to 1.43 Mb / 20 genes South of atp1b1a) contained no nonsense, non-conservative missense or splice site mutations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: atp1b1a encodes a β-subunit of a Na,K-ATPase.
source: atp1b1a encodes a β-subunit of a Na,K-ATPase, an ion pump that drives the directional transport of Na and K ions across cell membranes.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the function of atp1b1a.

claim: Na,K-ATPase is an ion pump that drives the directional transport of Na and K ions across cell membranes.
source: atp1b1a encodes a β-subunit of a Na,K-ATPase, an ion pump that drives the directional transport of Na and K ions across cell membranes.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Na,K-ATPase function.

claim: The functional Na,K-ATPase pump consists of a catalytically active α-subunit and a regulatory β-subunit.
source: The functional pump consists of two subunits, the catalytically active α-subunit and the regulatory β-subunit, which is a type II transmembrane protein.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about Na,K-ATPase structure.

claim: The β-subunit of Na,K-ATPase is a type II transmembrane protein.
source: The functional pump consists of two subunits, the catalytically active α-subunit and the regulatory β-subunit, which is a type II transmembrane protein.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the β-subunit structure.

claim: The C to T transition (C760T) results in the generation of a premature stop codon (Q254*).
source: The identified C to T transition (C760T) results in the generation of a premature stop codon (Q254*) (Figure 3d), removing the highly conserved C-terminus of the β-subunit's extracellular domain.
evidence: The claim is supported by the sequence analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The premature stop codon removes the highly conserved C-terminus of the β-subunit's extracellular domain.
source: The identified C to T transition (C760T) results in the generation of a premature stop codon (Q254*) (Figure 3d), removing the highly conserved C-terminus of the β-subunit's extracellular domain.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the location of the stop codon and knowledge of protein structure.

claim: Knocking down atp1b1a in wild-type embryos with a MO produces edema and epidermal phenotypes indistinguishable from those of the psoriasis mutants.
source: Upon knocking down atp1b1a in wild-type embryos with a previously described MO blocking atp1b1a translation (Blasiole et al., 2006), we obtained edema and epidermal phenotypes indistinguishable from those of the psoriasis mutants (Figure 3e).
evidence: The claim is supported by morpholino knockdown data shown in Figure 3e and cites Blasiole et al., 2006 for the MO.

claim: The identified mutation in atp1b1a is the causative lesion.
source: This indicates that the identified mutation is indeed the causative lesion and has a loss-of-function effect.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phenocopy experiment with the morpholino.

claim: The identified mutation in atp1b1a has a loss-of-function effect.
source: This indicates that the identified mutation is indeed the causative lesion and has a loss-of-function effect.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the phenocopy experiment with the morpholino and the nature of the premature stop codon.

claim: atp1b1a is strongly expressed in the pronephros at 24-48 hpf.
source: Consistent with former reports (Thisse et al., 2001), atp1b1a was strongly expressed in the pronephros, the heart, and multiple (other) epithelia (Figure 3f,g).
evidence: The claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 3f,g and cites Thisse et al., 2001.

claim: atp1b1a is strongly expressed in the heart at 24-48 hpf.
source: Consistent with former reports (Thisse et al., 2001), atp1b1a was strongly expressed in the pronephros, the heart, and multiple (other) epithelia (Figure 3f,g).
evidence: The claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 3f,g and cites Thisse et al., 2001.

claim: atp1b1a is strongly expressed in multiple epithelia at 24-48 hpf.
source: Consistent with former reports (Thisse et al., 2001), atp1b1a was strongly expressed in the pronephros, the heart, and multiple (other) epithelia (Figure 3f,g).
evidence: The claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 3f,g and cites Thisse et al., 2001.

claim: atp1b1a is expressed in peridermal cells.
source: In addition, we found previously unrecognized expression in peridermal cells, but not in the basal keratinocytes of the epidermis (Figure 3h,i).
evidence: The claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 3h,i.

claim: atp1b1a is not expressed in the basal keratinocytes of the epidermis.
source: In addition, we found previously unrecognized expression in peridermal cells, but not in the basal keratinocytes of the epidermis (Figure 3h,i).
evidence: The claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 3h,i.

claim: The zebrafish Na,K-ATPase α-subunit Atp1a1a.1 is required for heart tube elongation.
source: The zebrafish Na,K-ATPase α-subunit Atp1a1a.1 has been formerly described as required for heart tube elongation and proper heart-beating (Cheng et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim cites Cheng et al., 2003 as the source of this information.

claim: The zebrafish Na,K-ATPase α-subunit Atp1a1a.1 is required for proper heart-beating.
source: The zebrafish Na,K-ATPase α-subunit Atp1a1a.1 has been formerly described as required for heart tube elongation and proper heart-beating (Cheng et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim cites Cheng et al., 2003 as the source of this information.

claim: psoriasis mutants display a mildly reduced heartbeat rate at 33 hpf.
source: psoriasis mutants also displayed a mildly reduced heartbeat rate at 33 hpf, which was more pronounced at 50 hpf (Figure 4c), but no defects in heart tube elongation were apparent at 34 hpf (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by heartbeat rate measurements shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The reduced heartbeat rate in psoriasis mutants is more pronounced at 50 hpf.
source: psoriasis mutants also displayed a mildly reduced heartbeat rate at 33 hpf, which was more pronounced at 50 hpf (Figure 4c), but no defects in heart tube elongation were apparent at 34 hpf (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by heartbeat rate measurements shown in Figure 4c.

claim: No defects in heart tube elongation are apparent in psoriasis mutants at 34 hpf.
source: psoriasis mutants also displayed a mildly reduced heartbeat rate at 33 hpf, which was more pronounced at 50 hpf (Figure 4c), but no defects in heart tube elongation were apparent at 34 hpf (Figure 4a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 4a,b.

claim: atp1b1a is required for proper functioning of the embryonic heart rather than for its development.
source: This suggests that atp1b1a is required for proper functioning of the embryonic heart rather than for its development, although the cellular basis of the heart malfunction in psoriasis mutants remains unclear.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that heart tube elongation is normal but heart beating is reduced.

claim: The cellular basis of the heart malfunction in psoriasis mutants remains unclear.
source: This suggests that atp1b1a is required for proper functioning of the embryonic heart rather than for its development, although the cellular basis of the heart malfunction in psoriasis mutants remains unclear.
evidence: The claim is an explicit statement of uncertainty.

claim: Antibodies raised against chicken Na,K-ATPase α-subunits α5 and α6F detect zebrafish α-isoforms in the embryonic kidney.
source: Antibodies raised against the chicken Na,K-ATPase α-subunits α5 and α6F have been reported to detect zebrafish α-isoforms in the embryonic kidney (Drummond et al., 1998) and in ionocytes (Lin et al., 2006) (but not in the heart and periderm; own data not shown).
evidence: The claim cites Drummond et al., 1998 as the source of this information.

claim: Antibodies raised against chicken Na,K-ATPase α-subunits α5 and α6F detect zebrafish α-isoforms in ionocytes.
source: Antibodies raised against the chicken Na,K-ATPase α-subunits α5 and α6F have been reported to detect zebrafish α-isoforms in the embryonic kidney (Drummond et al., 1998) and in ionocytes (Lin et al., 2006) (but not in the heart and periderm; own data not shown).
evidence: The claim cites Lin et al., 2006 as the source of this information.

claim: Antibodies raised against chicken Na,K-ATPase α-subunits α5 and α6F do not detect zebrafish α-isoforms in the heart and periderm.
source: Antibodies raised against the chicken Na,K-ATPase α-subunits α5 and α6F have been reported to detect zebrafish α-isoforms in the embryonic kidney (Drummond et al., 1998) and in ionocytes (Lin et al., 2006) (but not in the heart and periderm; own data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' own unpublished data.

claim: α5/α6F immunolabelling is completely absent in the pronephric duct of psoriasis mutants.
source: α5/α6F immunolabelling was completely absent in the pronephric duct of psoriasis mutants, but not in their ionocytes (Figure 4g–j), demonstrating that the mutation in the β-subunit results in a complete failure to target these α-subunits to the basolateral membrane of pronephric cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4g-j.

claim: α5/α6F immunolabelling is present in ionocytes of psoriasis mutants.
source: α5/α6F immunolabelling was completely absent in the pronephric duct of psoriasis mutants, but not in their ionocytes (Figure 4g–j), demonstrating that the mutation in the β-subunit results in a complete failure to target these α-subunits to the basolateral membrane of pronephric cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4g-j.

claim: The mutation in the β-subunit results in a complete failure to target α-subunits to the basolateral membrane of pronephric cells.
source: α5/α6F immunolabelling was completely absent in the pronephric duct of psoriasis mutants, but not in their ionocytes (Figure 4g–j), demonstrating that the mutation in the β-subunit results in a complete failure to target these α-subunits to the basolateral membrane of pronephric cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the absence of α5/α6F immunolabelling in the pronephric duct.

claim: Mislocalization of α-subunits in the zebrafish pronephros has been associated with compromised osmoregulatory function and edema formation.
source: A comparable mislocalization of α-subunits in the zebrafish pronephros has been associated with compromised osmoregulatory function and edema formation in several other instances (Drummond et al., 1998; Hentschel et al., 2005; Martin-Belmonte and Perez-Moreno, 2012).
evidence: The claim cites Drummond et al., 1998; Hentschel et al., 2005; Martin-Belmonte and Perez-Moreno, 2012 as sources of this information.

claim: The osmoregulatory demands of an animal depend on its environmental conditions.
source: The osmoregulatory demands of an animal depend on its environmental conditions.
evidence: The claim is based on general biological knowledge.

claim: Zebrafish have an estimated internal osmolarity of 230-300 mOsm.
source: Zebrafish live in freshwater and are estimated to have an internal osmolarity of 230–300 mOsm, whereas freshwater has 10 mOsms (Enyedi et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim cites Enyedi et al., 2013 as the source of this information.

claim: Freshwater has an osmolarity of 10 mOsm.
source: Zebrafish live in freshwater and are estimated to have an internal osmolarity of 230–300 mOsm, whereas freshwater has 10 mOsms (Enyedi et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim cites Enyedi et al., 2013 as the source of this information.

claim: Zebrafish embryos face a continuous passive influx of water due to external hypotonicity.
source: As a consequence of this external hypotonicity, the embryos face a continuous passive influx of water that needs to be actively excreted via the pronephros.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the osmotic gradient between the embryo and freshwater.

claim: Water influx in zebrafish embryos needs to be actively excreted via the pronephros.
source: As a consequence of this external hypotonicity, the embryos face a continuous passive influx of water that needs to be actively excreted via the pronephros.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of osmoregulation in freshwater fish.

claim: Compromised function of Atp1b1a in pronephros and heart causes edema formation as a result of increased water content.
source: Therefore, compromised function of Atp1b1a in pronephros and heart causes edema formation as a result of increased water content, which is indicative of hypotonicity in interstitual compartments.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the osmoregulatory defects and observed edema.

claim: Edema formation in psoriasis mutants is indicative of hypotonicity in interstitial compartments.
source: Therefore, compromised function of Atp1b1a in pronephros and heart causes edema formation as a result of increased water content, which is indicative of hypotonicity in interstitual compartments.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the relationship between water content and osmolarity.

claim: Incubation of psoriasis mutant embryos in E3 medium containing 250 mM mannitol leads to abrogation of edema formation.
source: To bypass the need for Atp1b1a for osmoregulation, we incubated psoriasis mutant embryos in E3 medium containing 250 mM mannitol, which is isotonic to the interior of the embryo (Enyedi et al., 2013). This treatment led to the expected abrogation of edema formation (Figure 5a–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5a-d and cites Enyedi et al., 2013 for the isotonicity of the medium.

claim: E3 medium containing 250 mM mannitol is isotonic to the interior of the zebrafish embryo.
source: To bypass the need for Atp1b1a for osmoregulation, we incubated psoriasis mutant embryos in E3 medium containing 250 mM mannitol, which is isotonic to the interior of the embryo (Enyedi et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim cites Enyedi et al., 2013 as the source of this information.

claim: Incubation of psoriasis mutant embryos in isotonic medium completely rescues epidermal hyperplasia and aggregate formation.
source: In addition and more surprisingly, it also completely rescued epidermal hyperplasia and aggregate formation (Figure 5a–k).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5a-k.

claim: Similar results to mannitol treatment are obtained by incubating mutant embryos in isotonic Ringer's solution.
source: Similar results were obtained by incubating mutant embryos in isotonic Ringer's solution (Figure 5i).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5i.

claim: Deregulation of the osmotic state in psoriasis mutants results in epidermal hyperplasia.
source: This indicates that deregulation of the osmotic state in psoriasis mutants results in epidermal hyperplasia, and that the osmoregulatory function of atp1b1a is required for proper epidermal homeostasis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue of epidermal hyperplasia by isotonic conditions.

claim: The osmoregulatory function of atp1b1a is required for proper epidermal homeostasis.
source: This indicates that deregulation of the osmotic state in psoriasis mutants results in epidermal hyperplasia, and that the osmoregulatory function of atp1b1a is required for proper epidermal homeostasis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue of epidermal hyperplasia by isotonic conditions.

claim: Wild-type embryos treated with 3mM ouabain display pericardial edema.
source: To test this, we incubated wild-type embryos in 3 mM ouabain, an inhibitor of the pumping function of the α-subunit. Treated embryos displayed numerous formerly reported phenotypes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; and data not shown), typical of those caused by genetic mutations in other Na,K-ATPases (Blasiole et al., 2006), as well as pericardial edema (Figure 5l–n).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5l-n.

claim: Wild-type embryos treated with 3mM ouabain do not develop epidermal aggregates.
source: These embryos did not, however, develop epidermal aggregates (Figure 5n', compare to Figure 5m'), indicating that the loss of the osmoregulatory function of Atp1b1a is necessary but not sufficient for epidermal hyperplasia.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5n'.

claim: The loss of the osmoregulatory function of Atp1b1a is necessary but not sufficient for epidermal hyperplasia.
source: These embryos did not, however, develop epidermal aggregates (Figure 5n', compare to Figure 5m'), indicating that the loss of the osmoregulatory function of Atp1b1a is necessary but not sufficient for epidermal hyperplasia.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that ouabain treatment causes edema but not epidermal aggregates.

claim: Loss of osmoregulatory function points to an additional, pump-independent function of Atp1b1a that makes keratinocytes more resistant to hypotonic stress.
source: This points to an additional, pump-independent function of Atp1b1a, which makes keratinocytes more resistant to hypotonic stress.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the necessity of both osmoregulatory defects and another function for epidermal malignancy.

claim: Na,K-ATPases have a role in epithelial polarity that promotes basolateral membrane identities.
source: Several functions additional to their role in ion homeostasis have been described for Na,K-ATPases, such as a role in epithelial polarity that promotes basolateral membrane identities, as well as a role in intercellular adhesion (see Introduction).
evidence: The claim refers to information provided in the Introduction section.

claim: Na,K-ATPases have a role in intercellular adhesion.
source: Several functions additional to their role in ion homeostasis have been described for Na,K-ATPases, such as a role in epithelial polarity that promotes basolateral membrane identities, as well as a role in intercellular adhesion (see Introduction).
evidence: The claim refers to information provided in the Introduction section.

claim: Atp1b1a-GFP is localized in the basolateral domain of peridermal cells.
source: To study the subcellular localization of zebrafish Atp1b1a, we transiently expressed an atp1b1a-gfp fusion construct in peridermal cells, one of its endogenous expression sites (Figure 3i), under the control of the krt4 promoter. As described for Na,K-ATPases in other epithelial cells, Atp1b1a-GFP was localized in the basolateral domain of peridermal cells, together with E-cadherin (Cdh1), while it was absent from the apical region marked by the tight junction protein Tjp1/ZO-1 (Kiener and Hunziker, 2007) (Figure 6a).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6a and cites Kiener and Hunziker, 2007.

claim: Atp1b1a-GFP co-localizes with E-cadherin (Cdh1) in peridermal cells.
source: As described for Na,K-ATPases in other epithelial cells, Atp1b1a-GFP was localized in the basolateral domain of peridermal cells, together with E-cadherin (Cdh1), while it was absent from the apical region marked by the tight junction protein Tjp1/ZO-1 (Kiener and Hunziker, 2007) (Figure 6a).

claim: Atp1b1a-GFP is absent from the apical region of peridermal cells marked by Tjp1/ZO-1.
